Who so sincerely minds it.

2 Marriage, a point of our rest,
As it rightly may be called,
The pleasure of loving desires,
And Love that is not ashamed.

3 When one binds oneself in marriage;
Here going to unite with a Woman,
One rightly marries there,
Granting the marriage bond.

4 Dear ones, wish to stay together,
Let no sadness be seen here,
Here is the reward of sweet courtship,
Let us wish this couple happiness.

5 Lord Groom and Lady Bride elevated,
I wish you happiness and much prosperity,
That God may give you His blessing,
And His grace in abundance.

6 Groom, wish to love your Bride,
And give honor to the weak,
Therefore always be of one mind,
Live peacefully with her according to God's Teachings.

7 Bride, also wish to strive for this,
And live with your Man in peace,
Wish to call and regard him your Lord,
Just as Sarah did Abraham.

8 I wish that from your offspring,
By God, you may obtain children,
And that by God's grace,
You may raise them for your joy.

9 Those may be a source of happiness for you,
And be very pleasant to you,
Praised at your table and feast,
That we all wish you together.", 'Nimphjes come, awake now  
And weave a wreath of laurels,  
And therewith adorn the heads  
Of this sweet blessed pair.  
2 Who have entered into marriage together,  
And are firmly bound by faithfulness,  
See how rightly our bridegroom  
Has found his dearest one.  
Address to the Bridegroom.  
3 A worthy pledge, a great treasure  
Born from God for your delight,  
Which scarcely can be understood,  
Chosen from many thousands.  
4 A wife, a wife to your liking,  
A mutual pledge of great value,  
With which you accept the marriage for your rest,  
Through love and faithfulness.  
5 Your second soul, your only fate,  
With whom you hope to live from now on,  
Who from the Lord your God  
Is given to you for your comfort.  
6 Just as Christ the head very well  
Is praised by His congregation,  
So, bridegroom, you must  
Know that she is the head of your wife.  
7 Rule her with good understanding,  
Always be peaceful with her,  
Know that for this reason the marriage bond  
Exists out of love and faithfulness.  
Address to the Bride.  
8 Wife, consider your husband dear and worthy,  
Never speak harsh words to him,  
Remember that you are paired for this reason,  
To live peacefully with him.  
9 Call your husband Lord like Sarah,  
Govern your household in order,  
For if you follow her here,  
You become her daughter.  
10 Always persevere in God’s teaching,  
Let your deeds be honorably begun,  
For through the chastity of women,  
Many a man has often been won.  
Guests to the Bridegroom and Bride.  
11 Be united like Ennias,  
Who had his wife for forty-three years  
Without either of them  
Being quarrelsome.  
12 And if you receive children from the Lord,  
Raise them according to God’s pleasure,  
In His holy teaching,  
That you may see good days from her.  
13 This we all wish for you,  
That God’s grace and great blessing,  
In abundance from year to year,  
Descend upon you like fruitful rain.', 'Who is there, joyful in spirit,
Who does not gladly raise his song of praise,
On this so joyful feast,
Of Bridegroom and Bride!
The Couple, who meets our eye here,
Is truly worthy of that praise,
May they remain in prosperity and adversity
Long saved for each other. repeat.

Enjoy, O Bridegroom and Bride!
The greatest happiness on earth,
That nothing ever hinders your delight,
Freed from disaster and distress,

Step happily into the marriage boat,
It carries you along a smooth path,
Sincere loyalty and marital love
Scatter roses along your way. repeat.

Live contentedly, healthy and happy,
Many years together,
May every day be blessed,
Your blessed state undisturbed;
Marital bliss increase your joy,
Though it be your fate on earth,
And remain as a reward for your virtue,
Long paired together. repeat.']

Name: 4_young wife_maidens_young maiden_maiden
Representative_Docs:
["Last year I took my young wife  
The year before last, the other half  
I took her to a tender hayfield  
Down to the village meadow  
She mowed hay, jingled in the forest  
Took a breath, caught in the forest  
The willow branch cracked  
Mowed a meadow, mowed two  
Started the third mowing place  
She immediately began to wilt  
Her eyes began to wither  
Started to ache in the knees  
To lie down like a sick sow  
Lost her shoelaces  
Complained about her heels  
I went to the old woman's prayer  
Oh, my dear old woman  
The wife became sweetly ill  
Started aching in the knees  
To lie down like a sick sow  
Lost her shoelaces  
So look after, young lad  
Take the barley to the threshing floor  
Carry the oats to the barn  
The rye to the flax field  
Then we will slaughter the lambs  
Then we will fry the ducklings  
We will put the firewood by the stove  
Strike the blows on the thigh  
Between the white horns.", 'I saw the maiden growing;
By the blue fence
Swelling with a red wreath;
Rising in a tin crown.
I, from the stables;
From the coal-black haven,
From the window I gave barley,
In the shadows I carried water;
Without the old woman's knowledge,
Without the old man's knowledge,
That I gained the horse's strength.
In front I put sturdy irons;
Behind irons from the threshing floor.
Then I harnessed the horse.
After that I put on the bridle,
On top I put a playful bow,
Eyes into silk reins,
Eyebrows into golden rings,
Tail into a braid,
Brushed the mane to one side.
I rode to the father-in-law's door,
I rode to the mother-in-law's door:
"Hello, father-in-law! Boot-tops,
Hello, mother-in-law! Neck of the kettle,
Are your maidens at home?"
The mother-in-law understood, answered:
"Our daughters are at the well,
Drawing water at the well."
I ride to the well road:
"Hello, dear maiden!
Drawing water with the bucket,
To water all the village's herd;
To water my horse at the well.
Let my black one paw,
Let my gray one sway,
Let my dappled one tug,
Move on the linen cloth.
I, a poor wayfarer,
Wayfarer, knower of lands;
Lord of matters,
Messenger of kings,
Keeper of the town council's book,
A postman from St. Petersburg."
The maiden hears, answers again:
"You are not a poor wayfarer,
Wayfarer, knower of lands,
Lord of matters,
Messenger of kings,
Keeper of the town council's book,
Postman from St. Petersburg.
You are an evil suitor,
And a deceitful groom:
Why is your horse harnessed?
Brushed mane and swayed tail?
Why do you have locks on the bridle?
Why do you have an eagle's skull?
A headgear in the harness?
A sparrow in the reins?"
I heard, answered again,
"I have at home an old father
Who makes the locks on the bridle.
I have at home a little brother
Who is my horse's groom,
Brushed mane and swayed tail.
He puts the tail in a braid,
Eyes in silk reins,
Ears in golden rings.
I have at home a little sister
Who makes the letters on gloves
Who makes lace on the whip..."', 'Last year I took a young wife  
The year before, another partner  
She was plump and red  
She was pale and sickly  
She was healthy and sharp  
I took her to the tender hayfield  
To the dry, golden meadow  
She mowed hay, rustled the forest  
Took the swath, caught in the forest  
Took the bow, took the two  
Slept on the third  
Put her apron under her head;  
The apron strings as a pillow  
The apron straps as bedding  
I went home crying:  
Under the stable yard  
The woman came out to meet me, the old man came out to meet me  
Immediately asking me:  
Why do you cry, young lad?  
Why should I cry, old lady?  
Or why should I cry, old man?  
I answered, I told:  
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before, another partner  
She was plump and red  
She was pale and sickly  
She was healthy and sharp  
I took her to the tender hayfield  
To the dry, golden meadow  
She mowed hay, rustled the forest  
Took the swath, caught in the forest  
Took the bow, took the two  
Slept on the third  
Put her apron under her head  
The apron strings as a pillow  
The apron straps as bedding  
She began to limp!  
From the pig seller to sleep  
From the shoelace to shrivel  
From the sole to fall  
The old woman replied, answering:  
Oh, you crazy young lad!  
Oh, you crazy and foolish  
Throw the city girls away  
Barley rolled directly  
Oats following in pairs  
Do one deed without alcohol  
Half a vat of moonshine;  
Five vats of beer  
Oh, woman is ale’s delight:  
Sharp woman is beer’s joy,  
Plague woman is beer barrel’s pleasure;  
Then the woman will be healthy!  
Like other women. -']

Name: 5_praise honor_virtue_praise_salvation
Representative_Docs:
["1.  
What cause may God give,  
That He lets us prosper  
In peace for so many years?  
His desire for our well-being.  

2.  
This never-deserved blessing  
Produces in us every day  
The fruit of bearing here,  
By walking in God's ways.  

3.  
You can clearly see here,  
That never gaining virtue,  
But always keeping earthly desires  
Is dangerous.  

4.  
Oh, turn once inward,  
And is today  
Even better than the past,  
Your soul will find rest.  

5.  
This I hope from you,  
Not only but moreover,  
That you increasingly  
Are penetrated to walk to God.  

6.  
The moderate effort,  
Many think is enough:  
Thus youth goes astray too soon,  
And was (Alas) deceived.  

7.  
But so as not to stray,  
I wish that you may renounce  
Early the enjoyment of earthly show,  
And draw comfort from above.  

8.  
Oh! Whoever has grasped this well,  
By insight finding some pleasure,  
God creates in holy bearing,  
For no treasure gives such a treasure.  

9.  
When I deeply consider this here,  
Though I am saddened,  
That I still need  
To seek to strengthen you.  

10.  
It is true for you all the years,  
If God has also commanded,  
What the body needs  
To skillfully gather as food.  

11.  
The earthly, only perishable,  
Cannot nourish you, O human;  
The soul must be guarded  
Eternal and immortal.  

12.  
The most important thing here is,  
To follow the Spirit's counsel,  
And reject the flesh’s advice:  
Let this also weigh the heaviest.  

13.  
Gather such treasures,  
By which (though you forsake  
All that flesh once enjoys)  
You are embraced by God.  

14.  
Whoever wants to lose all this  
For my sake and life,  
Says Christ, to give for me,  
I choose to be my servant.  

15.  
Granted to you by God many goods;  
Feeds; Refreshes; Clothes; and Shelters;  
Visits; and comes unbidden  
To your imprisoned brothers.  

16.  
Thus if you here so generously  
Lay away against what is coming,  
A firm ground departing,  
You will find God gracious.  

17.  
In short, if you want to sow here so,  
Not to the flesh destruction,  
But to the Spirit; as inheritance  
You will reap eternal life.  

18.  
Grant that we may with confidence  
Oh! Lord, daily follow You:  
Gather Youth and Virtue:  
And afterward behold You.", "If you wish to be a Warrior,  
A Camper, a Knight of the Lord,  
Let yourself be marked, put on arms,  
You must learn to fight and battle.  

2. For we have here no struggle  
Against flesh and common blood:  
But against the pride of the wide world,  
We must fight, great and small.  

3. Against Kings and great Princes,  
All who govern darkness,  
We must fight unto death,  
Upright with pious Christ’s banner.  

4. Cunning, worse than venom,  
Of spirits who work in the air,  
We must also be fighting,  
Noting their wickedness and deceit.  

5. They can perform signs and wonders,  
And by an appearance lie the truth,  
Those who do not hold firmly to Christ  
They will deceive all of them.  

6. Let us hope with good patience,  
Leaving behind evil manners,  
So that God on the evil day,  
May well govern through His Spirit.  

7. In a body subject to sin  
Does not dwell God’s Spirit, free from discord,  
Nor does He enter any soul  
Disobedient and evil of will.  

8. But he who seeks Christ early and late,  
To serve without ceasing,  
Shall receive and be free from shame,  
If he does not temper Him.  

9. He will put on their strong weapons,  
(With which he has conquered all)  
And must give, for it is his work,  
Victory he will grant them.  

Pause.  

10. Thus stand, be pious in your fight,  
Gird your loins with truth,  
Put on the breastplate well and upright,  
Righteousness without hardship.  

11. Be shod on your feet well  
With the Gospel of peace,  
To run swiftly as a messenger,  
Messages of God's mercies.  

12. Take faith as a shield  
Against the devil’s unruliness,  
Whereby all his fiery darts  
Are quenched and silenced.  

13. The helmet of salvation you will wisely  
Also place upon your head,  
Grasp the sword of the Spirit, which is God’s word,  
To strike down your enemies.  

14. Bear Christ’s sign, the red cross,  
Willingly go out to the field with Him,  
Suffer shame, pressure, fear, death with confusion,  
Thus take His kingdom with power.  

15. Wish to walk with patience,  
Enduring, without any longing,  
In the fight God leads you,  
Thank, praise, and glorify Him with joyful songs.  

16. Wish to beg, pray in the Spirit,  
And keep good watch at all times,  
Do not flee from suffering or tempest,  
You will be found a true Knight.  

17. For those who flee from the fight,  
Will not please God:  
But those who fight steadfastly  
Until death, without despairing.  

18. They shall wash away their tears,  
Their suffering will be healed,  
They shall put on shining clothes white and clear,  
And be joyful.  

19. A crown (with greater melody)  
Christ shall also give upon their head,  
That will be their wage and their soldier’s pay,  
Here above in eternal life.", '1.  
The Christian’s highest duty,  
Of which God’s word speaks,  
Can never be more perfect,  
Than that they steadfastly  
Sharpen the mind  
To do good,  
To fear God earnestly.

2.  
Is it always good, even more so,  
Now since the Lord  
Enriches your years anew,  
That you are mindful  
That with this new time,  
New virtue must also accompany.

3.  
This is my wish and prayer,  
That soul’s and body’s pain  
Never disturb your rest here,  
Which you find in God; and especially,  
If through the Spirit,  
You are reborn in every way.

4.  
No one is moved to this,  
But death of earthly lease,  
And anything that the flesh desires:  
Unless one violently  
Suppresses the flesh’s passions,  
The spirit here never truly rests.

5.  
Seek the heavenly, the earthly perishes,  
Learn to die before you die,  
So that when the hour of death  
Suddenly comes upon you,  
You do not then learn to refuse the evil,  
(that now is the time).

6.  
Flee foolish pride,  
And foolish vanity:  
Much rather be present  
In spirit, and go inward,  
For inner adornment  
Is precious in God’s eyes.

7.  
Never let unfruitful words  
Depart from your lips,  
They offend pious ears:  
But produce all that has edification,  
So that it gives  
Grace to those who hear it.

8.  
Narrow is the path of life,  
Nothing unclean has hold there:  
So do not seek space where it is narrow:  
God’s word is easily misinterpreted  
According to the flesh’s convenience:  
Whereby one becomes slow and lukewarm.

9.  
Is it then sinful  
To act joyfully?  
Oh no, I would not say that:  
Yet I find it necessary  
That joy originates,  
From God, I return to Him.

10.  
Now that the Spirit lives,  
Strive to celebrate the best,  
Endeavor to imitate Christ,  
So you are refreshed in Him,  
And keep watch for His coming,  
You will find heaven on earth.

11.  
Oh, sweet slavery!  
Who is freer?  
Than one who is bowed before God,  
Enjoys Him here in hope,  
Sees the freedom to come,  
With spiritual eyes.

12.  
This I now wish for you,  
That you grow weary of the world,  
Desire only God:  
And withdraw your mind  
From earthly goods,  
And for God, lack everything.

13.  
Ah Lord! grant that we  
May continuously lift up  
Our hearts and eyes to You;  
And watch in the Spirit,  
To be with You here and especially  
To enjoy You hereafter.']

Name: 6_sailors_sailing_sail_set sail
Representative_Docs:
["Who wants to hear a New Song
Exalted from our Fishermen,
Listen well to my message,
Those who venture on the North Sea,
Without fear or trembling,
With brave courage,
And stake their lives,
In God's keeping,
On the open Sea,
To do each according to his diligence
And very gladly,
Return home.
Friends, our Ship is already prepared,
If God will but give a good Wind,
We sail all guided by God,
Uplifted in our trade,
To live together,
Holy according to God's Word,
As it may please,
Always forward and onward,
To God's delight
With courage always,
To do our diligence,
Our days of life.
Farewell now, dear Friends,
Who inhabit our City,
We commend you all to God,
Young and old People,
As we now part,
For a short time,
May the Lord lead you,
And bless you with health;
Farewell Father and
Mother,
Sisters and Brothers all,
Trust indeed,
In God our Keeper.
We sail all in good spirits,
With a good Wind uplifted,
We hope in God's keeping,
To set out for that purpose,
Like the honorable Apostles,
Together following Christ's words,
To Fish on the Sea,
As they have done,
According to Matthew's teaching,
Casting the Net to the right side,
With Peter joyfully,
On the Word of the Lord.
When we come to the northern Sand,
We shoot our Herring-net,
We then put it in God's hand,
To enjoy the Herring,
Listen to my testimony,
We get a good Catch,
We shoot with pleasure,
Our Corner-net quickly,
Without delay,
Each doing his diligence,
With glad courage,
To our liking.
If we get a good catch of Fish,
Then we rejoice,
We thank the Lord for sure,
And put pressure aside,
Without long hesitation,
If they then drop anchor,
Then we prepare ourselves,
With a very cheerful heart,
To sleep a while,
And that does not last very long,
We move along,
Again with the Boys.
Thus we continue our Trade,
Until the Voyage ends,
We live according to God's Holy Word,
May He send us His blessing,
But if we do otherwise,
God will withdraw His hand,
And His gentle blessing,
From us for
He will reveal
Whoever acts against His will,
It is not good,
To sail this way.
If we get Storm and also Thunder,
As often happens,
Protect us then,
O good Lord:
That no one regrets it,
In the great Sea distress,
Punish, the Waves ward off,
So that we do not as dead,
Discouraged Hearts stand,
But strengthen us,
As your good Disciples,
In the Sea-flood
They could endure.
When God then calms the Waves again,
And brings good Weather,
Very soon we take our turn,
With joy taken out
To our Trade once more,
With a peaceful life,
Until we return,
Again to reckon,
To our Friends in the Dutch valley,
With joyful cheer,
Come together.
When we then come ashore again,
With abundant blessing,
Everyone offers us their hand,
Speak kindheartedly,
Be welcome Friend with peace,
And honorable Ladies,
Do the same likewise,
To their Husbands truly,
The kind Parents,
To their Children at this time
Welcome joyfully,
They quickly shout.
Farewell then all you Fishermen together,
Who cultivate the North Sea,
I commend you in God's name,
Always trust in Him,
He will help you well,
Out of every heavy need,
Stay the Flood surely,
Although He makes a great clamor,
Without wavering
Always firmly hold to His Doctrine,
Then the Lord sends
His rich blessing.
Who first sang us this little Song,
It was a young man done,
Out of love for many young Fishermen,
He went to present this,
Sail well now uplifted,
You all Fishermen,
On the North Sea written,
I tell you truly,
The Year Sixteen Hundred,
And six times ten capable,
Farewell all together,
None excluded.", "Hear, sailors all together,
Who sail by the sea,
Whether you face storm or distress,
God will help you on a course:
For many a ship's mate,
Must risk their lives,
Alone on the sea's swell,
By nights and by days.
The sea, by God's will,
Devours so many men,
Who all together from the fish
Are then swallowed:
But read! What depends on that,
Where our bodies sail,
If God will then
Eternally preserve the soul.
What sorrow the seaman suffers,
By nights and by days,
When he sees death before his eyes,
And cannot escape it,
From storm and great thunder,
And the power of the waves,
That brings us thus all the more
Into fear and great distress.
Also great violence and adversity,
The seaman bravely suffers,
From Turks, ravaging pirates fierce,
They are attacked:
And many more enemies,
Who seek to harm,
Who sail by the sea
May well think of this.
Even when they are driven aground
By storms,
Very hastily they hew the masts,
Then cut overboard:
Then they see death again,
Before their eyes with dread,
Sometimes the sorrow is great,
That the seaman must bear.
God helps them then out of distress,
Who call to Him fervently,

For by His strong hand,

And brings them again to land
In a desired haven.

That the Lord has blessed them,
Faith helped by His grace,
